nodes.title: Note: MiniMax H3
widgets_values:
## MiniMax H3

[MiniMax H3](https://www.minimax.io/blog/minimax-h3) is MiniMax's general-purpose, omni-modal generation model. It jointly understands text, image, video, and audio, and generates video with **native stereo audio**: voice, sound effects, and music are modeled jointly in a single forward pass, not layered on afterward. Output is up to 2K resolution, 24fps, and up to about 15 seconds.

## ComfyUI links
- [ComfyUI#15224](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI/pull/15224)
- [🤗 Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3)

## About this workflow

This template runs the **reference-to-video (ref2va)** task using the `MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo` node. It takes any mix of reference images, videos, and standalone audio, and weaves them into the generation to lock in a character's identity, a style, a motion, a camera move, or a voice.

**Key inputs**

- **ref_images / ref_videos / ref_video_audios / ref_audios**: up to 9 reference images, 3 reference videos (each may carry its own paired soundtrack), and 3 standalone reference audio clips
- **prompt**: reference the inputs by tag, in the exact order they were connected, for example `<Picture 1>`, `<Video 1>`, `<Audio 1>`, then describe the target scene, motion, and audio
- **ref_image_size**: `match` scales references down to the generation's resolution (faster); `max` keeps up to a 2048px short edge for stronger identity fidelity, at the cost of speed since reference tokens ride along every sampling step
- **width / height**: set via Resolution Selector.
- **duration (seconds)**: converted to a valid frame `length` by the Math Expression node

**Sampling and decode**

- Sampler: `res_multistep`. `beta` or `normal` scheduler tends to outperform `simple` for reference-heavy prompts like this one
- The sampler's joint audio+video `LATENT` output feeds directly into both `VAEDecode` (video, `minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16`) and `VAEDecodeAudio` (audio, `minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32`); each decode node automatically pulls its own half out of the packed latent. `CreateVideo` then muxes the two into a single MP4 with synced sound
- The diffusion model here is `minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors`, a different set of weights from the `fl2va` model used by the t2v/i2v templates

Ref2va's output is very sensitive to prompt wording; matching the reference tags precisely and being explicit about which reference drives which part of the shot tends to work best.

subject_definitions:
<Picture 1> is the reference for the whole scene: a girl in a black cap with her long hair streaming, an oversized graphic tee, baggy cargo shorts and chunky sneakers, riding a sleek hoverboard platform with four glowing blue thruster pods mounted on articulated arms; a grey-and-white husky sits on the front of the board with its tongue hanging out and droplets flying off its muzzle, and the two of them race through a dark ruined futuristic environment of shattered concrete and drifting debris.

summary:
[reference generation] The girl and her husky blast forward on the hoverboard through the ruined streets, slalom hard around slabs of fallen concrete and thread a collapsing gap at speed, then launch off a ramp over a chasm and skid-land in a spray — the husky sneezing mid-air as they freeze.

retention_analysis:
<Picture 1> (appears in [Shot 1], [Shot 2], [Shot 3]): fully_preserved - the girl's black cap, streaming long hair, graphic tee, cargo shorts and chunky sneakers, the husky's grey-and-white coat and lolling tongue, the hoverboard with four blue-glowing thruster pods, and the dark ruined futuristic environment are retained throughout.

detailed_description:
The target video is a cinematic cyberpunk-action style with a dark desaturated palette cut by the cold blue glow of the thruster pods, drifting dust, motion streaks and flying grit.
Stage direction is fixed and never changes: the board travels only toward screen-right; the husky sits at the front of the board in the direction of travel and the girl stands behind it; the camera stays on the left-hand side of the board for the entire video and never crosses to the right-hand side or in front of the board's nose, so the direction of travel, the husky's position and the girl's stance stay consistent in every shot. Every droplet, spark and debris chip flies backward to screen-left as they move.
[Shot 1] A medium tracking shot from the board's left side. The camera trucks right with medium amplitude at fast speed, keeping pace as the girl throws her weight forward and the thrusters flare blue, the board surging off the mark; her hair and tee snap backward in the wind, the husky's jowls and ears flap wildly with its tongue streaming straight back, grit and dust whipping off the rear pods. She shouts over the roar (S1): <d>[中文] 抓紧了！</d>
[Shot 2] At 03.400s, from the same left-hand side, the camera keeps tracking right with large amplitude at very fast speed as she banks the board hard into a slalom, weaving between slabs of fallen concrete and clipping through a collapsing gap; a chunk of debris crashes down behind them in an explosion of dust, the thruster pods tilting and screaming, the husky's face wobbling comically as drool sprays sideways off its muzzle. She yells, laughing (S1): <d>[中文] 让开让开——！</d>
[Shot 3] At 06.800s, the camera pulls back and cranes up with large amplitude at fast speed as they hit a broken ramp and launch out over a chasm, the board hanging in the air for a long beat, thrusters roaring, the girl upright and grinning while the husky's tongue floats and a sneeze bursts from its nose in a fine spray of droplets. They slam down on the far side in a skidding drift, sparks screeching off the pods and dust fanning out as she straightens up. She looks down at the soaking husky and says, deadpan (S1): <d>[中文] ……它又打喷嚏了。</d> The frame freezes on the husky's derpy face.

overall_soundscape: The thruster pods whine and howl as they spool up and bank, wind rushes and buffets the mic, dust and grit hiss off the concrete, debris crashes down behind them with a heavy boom, the board screeches and sparks on the skid-landing, and the husky's sneeze squeaks out over the fading roar.

non_diegetic_music: A punchy electro-rock track with a driving synth bass, hand-clap backbeat and a distorted guitar riff at a fast tempo, a whoosh-riser on the ramp, a big crash accent on the landing, then a comedic record-scratch and a light tinkle on the husky's sneeze.
